title: Dimensions 2026: Turning project risk into confidence
summary: More than 7,000 industry professionals gathered at Trimble Dimensions 2026. Explore key announcements on AI, Trimble Connect, connected workflows and the future of construction.
body_markdown:
## Connecting teams to reduce project risk: Inside Dimensions 2026


For over 20 years, the construction professionals and innovators shaping our infrastructure have gathered at the[Trimble Dimensions user conference](https://www.trimble.com/en/our-company/events/dimensions/overview) . This year was no different, with over 7,000 attendees coming together at the Venetian Resort in Las Vegas. This year’s theme was a single word: **“Every”** .


Attendees came to Dimensions looking for ways to connect their teams, meet modern industry challenges and uncover new technology opportunities. This week delivered all of that in a collaborative space where they could learn directly from Trimble experts while networking with peers.


To set the tone for the three-day event, Trimble President and CEO Rob Painter took the mainstage and started with a simple observation: **The technology changed. The work didn’t.**


## Old habits and risky handoffs


Bringing complex projects to life still comes with friction. Bridging that disconnect starts with addressing one of the industry's biggest challenges: project risk.


In his keynote, Painter shared a number of familiar risks, emphasizing that the gap between teams, tools, and workflows is where most project risk originates today. If the problem is risk, what’s the solution? Many might point you toward a simple one: “update your technology”. But, as Painter explained in his example, technology alone isn’t always enough.


When factories first got electricity, they replaced their steam engines with electric motors but didn’t update their processes. The technology was there, but without reshaping the workflows around the new tech, its initial impact was marginal.


[AI is construction’s electricity moment](https://www.trimble.com/en/blog/trimble/article/agentic-ai-foundation-physical-industries) , and it’s already clear that real acceleration comes from ensuring the work evolves with the technology.


## AI and the Trimble Connect platform


Going back to the initial issue: risk that lives in the gaps. When Trimble introduced[Trimble Connect](https://www.trimble.com/en/products/trimble-connect) in 2014, it focused on bridging those gaps by giving teams a shared home to view and manage project files. Today, it has expanded to host over 55 million registered users and 35 million projects. A million monthly active users generate more than a petabyte of data every quarter, and thousands of connections run through its[Marketplace](https://marketplace.trimble.com/en-US/home) and APIs.


Now, with the intentional use of AI as an accelerator,[Trimble Connect has evolved](https://news.trimble.com/what-is-next-for-trimble-connect-by-rob-painter) to become a[centralized project platform.](https://www.trimble.com/en/solutions/platforms) Workflows customers already rely on are becoming capabilities on Connect, so their project data can move between them seamlessly.


AI powers the entire platform, connecting the three core elements Trimble has tracked for 48 years: **where** the project is, **what** it should be and **why** key decisions are made. By focusing on those decisions, Trimble AI catches risk before it turns into cost. And all of it runs on ground truth: precise measurement from the field that the office and the site can both trust.


As Rob put it, “In AI we believe. In ground truth we trust.”


## "How We Build Next"


Rob’s keynote made the case that the real gains come from redesigning how the work gets done.


“[How We Build Next: A Trimble Podcast](https://www.trimble.com/en/learn/how-we-build-next-podcast) ,” which was also announced at Dimensions 2026, asks the people doing that redesign what it takes. The video series starts from one question: What would construction look like if its people, data and workflows were connected, and what will it take to get there?


Four Trimble executives will co-host:[Mark Schwartz, group president, AECO](https://www.trimble.com/en/learn/how-we-build-next-podcast#general-1) ;[Heather Adkins, senior vice president and AECO chief marketing officer](https://www.trimble.com/en/learn/how-we-build-next-podcast#general-2) ;[Josh Levy, vice president of risk and compliance](https://www.trimble.com/en/learn/how-we-build-next-podcast#general-3) ; and[Boris Skopljak, senior vice president, geospatial](https://www.trimble.com/en/learn/how-we-build-next-podcast#general-4) . Guests will come from across construction and related industries.


The[trailer is out now](http://trimble.com/howwebuildnext.) , and full episodes are coming soon.


## Three days to learn, win and celebrate


The keynote set the stage for a week of innovation and connection. For the first time, Dimensions hosted a[Developer Summit](https://www.trimble.com/en/our-company/events/dimensions/developersummit) for software engineers and architects building on Trimble Connect, alongside the return of[3D Basecamp for SketchUp users](https://www.trimble.com/en/our-company/events/dimensions/3dbasecampsummit) . The opportunities to learn and grow didn’t stop there. Across the Venetian, attendees developed new skills in hands-on labs and met new cross-industry connections.


Some of those connections were forged in the spirit of competition. Finalists from[The Trimble 0-60 Challenge](https://www.trimble.com/en/our-company/events/dimensions/experiences/0-60-challenge) demoed early-stage solutions built on Trimble hardware and software. At the same time, the[10th annual Construction Startup Competition](https://constructionstartupcompetition.tech/) crowned its finalists after evaluating nearly 800 global entries. Alongside the startup showdowns, the[2026 Trimble Construction Innovation Awards](https://news.trimble.com/2026-11-04-Trimble-Announces-Winners-of-2026-Construction-Innovation-Awards) celebrated proven impact from industry leaders like F+F Mechanical, Wade Trim and HEI Civil, while also honoring top academic champions as Educators of the Year.


Meanwhile, out at the 15-acre[Offsite Expo](https://www.trimble.com/en/our-company/events/dimensions/offsiteexpo) , attendees ran heavy equipment, tested positioning tech in real-world simulations and watched autonomous machines work the site. Here, the connection between field operations and office workflows came to life. In active jobsite conditions, participants saw firsthand how real-time positioning and connected machine control transform raw field data into ground truth.


Getting hands-on experience with heavy machinery was just one of many ways to have fun at this year’s conference. Attendees relaxed with rescue dogs from Connect Pawsitively on the Expo floor, tackled a high-speed NASCAR pit crew tire swap at the Offsite Expo and wrapped up the week at OMNIA Nightclub for the multi-level customer appreciation party.


Much of these events took place under banners and digital signs reminding the attendees of the event’s key takeaway.


## …At every turn


Technology will keep changing. Measuring, designing and building will keep carrying risk. Dimensions 2026 showed that teams carry less of that risk when the office, the field and the shop work from the same ground truth on one platform to connect **Every** one, **Every** where, **Every** time.


As Rob put it in his closing statements, Trimble is “turning the risk in this industry into confidence.”


See how Trimble Connect bridges the gap between the field and the office and connects specialized workflows through one centralized platform.


[Learn more](https://www.trimble.com/en/products/trimble-connect)
